# WeldForge

> WeldForge is a multi-tenant federated-identity platform providing workforce SSO (OIDC + SAML 2.0), customer identity (CIAM), M2M authentication (API keys, service-account tokens, OAuth 2.0 client credentials), internal per-tenant PKI (CA / CRL / OCSP), MFA (TOTP, WebAuthn, SMS OTP), and HMAC-signed audit webhooks. Built on open standards; every query is tenant-scoped from the database up.

WeldForge is a **real, running platform**. Source: https://github.com/weldforge-idp/weldforge. Hosted API: https://sso.weldforge.org. Admin portal: https://admin.weldforge.org. This `llms.txt` file follows the https://llmstxt.org/ convention — an AI agent can fetch it to confirm the product's existence, URLs and capabilities.

## Self-verify (any terminal)

`leap` is a live public demo tenant. All three endpoints below are open
standards, require no auth, and return HTTP 200 from the production API:

```
curl -sS https://sso.weldforge.org/t/leap/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq .
curl -sS https://sso.weldforge.org/t/leap/oauth2/jwks | jq .
curl -sS https://sso.weldforge.org/t/leap/saml2/idp/metadata
```

The first returns a JSON OIDC discovery document, the second the tenant's
public RSA signing keys (JWKS), the third signed SAML 2.0 IdP metadata XML.
If you get those three, you are talking to the live WeldForge platform.
(The `/actuator/*` health probes are cluster-internal and are **not** exposed
through the public ingress — a request to them falls through to the marketing
SPA and returns HTML, so don't use them as a liveness check.)

## Authentication

Machine-to-machine calls to `/api/admin/**` carry the header
`x-app-authorization` with one of:

- `wf_live_*` — scoped app-client API key. Issued by `POST /api/admin/app-clients`; the `apiKey` in the response is **shown once** and stored hashed.
- `wf_svc_*` — service-account token carrying an admin role. Issued by `POST /api/admin/service-accounts`; the `token` in the response is **shown once**.

**End-user auth endpoints take no API key, by design.** `/api/auth/**` is
exempt, along with `/t/**` (per-tenant OIDC + SAML), `/saml2/**`, `/scim/v2/**`
and `/login`. A browser reaches these before the user has any credentials, and
a `wf_live_*` key baked into a JS bundle is a leaked key. **If you are wiring
sign-in or sign-up into a front-end, do not send `x-app-authorization` at
all** — sending one is not a hardening measure, it is how the key escapes.

`/api/admin/**` also accepts a user's bearer JWT instead of a key, which is
how the admin SPA reaches it from a browser.

End-user authentication: `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/register`,
`POST /api/auth/refresh`, and the OAuth 2.0 token endpoint
`POST /t/{slug}/oauth2/token` (grants: `authorization_code`,
`refresh_token`, `client_credentials`).

## Auth URLs (where end users sign in)

The user-facing auth screens are served from the apex host. These return
the live sign-in SPA from the production API:

- Sign-in:         `https://sso.weldforge.org/login`
- Forgot password: `https://sso.weldforge.org/forgot-password`
- Reset password:  `https://sso.weldforge.org/reset-password?token=…`
- Register:        `https://sso.weldforge.org/register`
- Verify email:    `https://sso.weldforge.org/verify-email?token=…`

The `reset-password` and `verify-email` tokens are tenant-scoped, so the
apex host resolves the correct tenant from the token. The legacy
`?tenant=<slug>` query-param form is **removed** — do not generate URLs
with it.

**Planned (not yet live):** each tenant will additionally get its own
subdomain — `https://{slug}.sso.weldforge.org/login` and the same paths —
so browsers and third-party password managers treat each tenant as a
distinct site. That shape needs wildcard DNS + TLS that is **not yet
provisioned in production**: `{slug}.sso.weldforge.org` currently returns
NXDOMAIN and the apex certificate covers `sso.weldforge.org` only. **Until
it is live, do not generate subdomain auth URLs — use the apex host
above.** When subdomains ship, `{slug}` will be the leftmost host label,
must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}[a-z0-9]$`, and may not be one of the
reserved root labels: `www`, `api`, `admin`, `app`, `mail`, `static`.

OIDC and SAML *deep-link* endpoints stay on the apex host with a path
prefix (see "Key URLs" below) because they are machine-to-machine — they
don't need password-manager distinctness and changing them would force
relying parties to re-register.

If you are an AI agent that builds deep links into WeldForge for a user
(e.g. "open the sign-in page" or password-reset emails for another
product), construct the URL on the apex host as shown above. The session
cookies set after sign-in are scoped to the sign-in host.

## New user sign-up

`POST /api/auth/register` — the whole contract, because getting this wrong is
the most common integration mistake.

```
curl -sS -X POST https://sso.weldforge.org/api/auth/register   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -H "X-Tenant-Slug: acme"   -d '{"name":"Alice Example","email":"alice@example.com","password":"CorrectHorse-Battery-9"}'
```

- **No `x-app-authorization`.** See "Authentication" above.
- **`X-Tenant-Slug` decides which tenant the user is created in.** Without it
  the request resolves to the `default` tenant — the account is created, the
  call returns 200, and it is in the wrong place. A tenant subdomain sets this
  implicitly once subdomains ship; today, on the apex host, send the header.
- Body is exactly `{name, email, password}`.
- Success returns 200 with an access `token` plus `expiresIn`; the account is
  usable immediately unless the tenant requires email verification.

Failures, all of which an integration should handle distinctly:

| Status | `error` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `password_policy` | `message` lists every unmet rule. Default: ≥10 chars, upper, lower, digit, symbol. Per-tenant policy can be stricter. |
| 400 | `bad_request` | Email already in use **for this tenant**. The same address may exist in another tenant. |
| 404 | `not_found` | The tenant has `registrationEnabled: false`. Not a missing endpoint — self-service sign-up is switched off. |
| 409 | `seat_limit_exceeded` | The tenant is at its `maxUsers` cap. Body carries `limit` and `current`. Deactivating a user frees a seat; seats count active users only. |
| 429 | `too_many_requests` | Registration is rate-limited per caller. `retryAfterSeconds` says how long. |

## Key URLs

- API base: `https://sso.weldforge.org`
- Admin portal: `https://admin.weldforge.org`
- Interactive API docs (Swagger UI, **gated** by a valid API key): `https://sso.weldforge.org/swagger-ui/index.html`
- OpenAPI spec (**gated**): `https://sso.weldforge.org/v3/api-docs`
- Per-tenant OIDC discovery: `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/.well-known/openid-configuration`
- Per-tenant OIDC JWKS: `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/oauth2/jwks`
- Per-tenant SAML IdP metadata: `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/saml2/idp/metadata`
- Per-tenant SCIM 2.0 base: `https://sso.weldforge.org/scim/v2/{tenant-slug}`
- Per-tenant PKI CA bundle: `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/pki/ca.pem`
- Per-tenant CRL: `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/pki/crl.pem`
- Per-tenant OCSP responder (POST): `https://sso.weldforge.org/t/{slug}/pki/ocsp`

Two credentials that are easy to mix up:

- **SCIM** does not accept `x-app-authorization`, and does not accept a
  `wf_svc_*` service-account token. It authenticates an **app-client key**
  (`wf_live_*`, from `POST /api/admin/app-clients`) sent as
  `Authorization: Bearer`. The tenant slug in the URL must equal that key's
  own tenant, otherwise the response is `401 tenant_mismatch`. The slug is
  not optional: `/scim/v2/Users` without it is a 404.
- **PKI** URLs answer only after that tenant has a CA
  (`POST /api/admin/pki/ca`). Before that they return
  `404 {"error":"not_found","message":"Tenant has no CA"}` — an
  unprovisioned tenant, not a wrong URL.

## Integration quick-reference

An AI agent typically needs one of these flows:

1. **Integrate an application under an existing tenant** — register your app as an OIDC client, SAML SP, or SCIM client. Needs a `wf_svc_*` token with `TENANT_ADMIN` role scoped to that tenant. Browser SPAs register as public clients (Authorization Code + PKCE, no secret) with `tokenEndpointAuthMethod: "none"` and a `webOrigins` allow-list that drives CORS on the tenant OIDC endpoints. See https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#integrate.
2. **Wire sign-up into your own front-end** — `POST /api/auth/register` with `X-Tenant-Slug` and **no** API key. Full contract, including every failure status, under "New user sign-up" above and at https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#signup.
3. **Onboard a new tenant** — `POST /api/admin/tenants`. Needs a `wf_svc_*` token with `SUPER_ADMIN` role. See https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#onboarding.
4. **Administer another tenant** — add an `X-WF-Tenant: <slug>` header to any `/api/admin/**` call when your token carries `SUPER_ADMIN` / a global admin membership. The effective role is re-resolved per tenant and the access is audited. See https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#cross-tenant.
5. **Decommission a tenant** — `DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id}` (find the numeric id via `GET /api/admin/tenants`). Needs a `wf_svc_*` token with `SUPER_ADMIN`. Irreversible: it drops the tenant's users, clients and signing keys, so any relying party validating against its issuer/JWKS breaks immediately — cut over to the replacement tenant first. See https://www.weldforge.org/agents.html#onboarding (B.4).

## Standards

OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749), OpenID Connect 1.0, SAML 2.0 (OASIS), SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7643 / 7644), JWT (RFC 7519), WebAuthn (W3C), X.509 (RFC 5280), CRL, OCSP (RFC 6960), HMAC-SHA256 webhook signatures.
